sentences.text: By this common impugned order dated 06/10/2015, both the claim cases were decided.
Both the appeals are being decided by the common order.
2. The brief facts of the case are that, on the date of incident i.e., 20/05/2013, the deceased Pankaj Pandey along with his friend, the injured Dilip Kumar was going to attend a wedding function.

Both of them stopped at a place to attend the call of nature, and during this time, the offending vehicle i.e.
Truck bearing registration No.CG-04-J-1455 dashed them which caused multiple injures to Pankaj Panday and he succumbed due to said injuries.
His colleague, Dilip Kumar Dwivedi also sustained multiple injuries and was admitted to the hospital for treatment.
3. The legal representatives of the deceased Pankaj Panday had preferred a claim petition seeking compensation to the tune of Rs. 1,46,27,552/-.
Injured Dilip Dwivedi also filed a claim petition for Divisional Manager vs Smt. Meera Pandey on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192986578/

sentences.text: 1 grant of compensation due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
After issuance of notice, the non-applicants entered appearance and filed their respective replies.

After framing of issues, the case proceeded for evidence, and thereafter, by the common award dated 06/10/2015, both the claim petitions were partly NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:58392 3 MA-749-2016 allowed by the learned Claims Tribunal.

4. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company criticised the award dated 06/10/ 2015 on the ground that initially, the FIR was lodged against an unknown vehicle and the pillion rider of the vehicle was not unconscious, therefore, no accident, as alleged before the Claim Tribunal had taken place.
It is further argued that the present incident is a concocted story and that accident was caused by an unknown vehicle and not by the offending vehicle.
It is further argued that the offending vehicle has been implanted in the incident in order to claim insurance amount.
Another limb of argument is that the quantum of compensation awarded is on higher side.
The salary and income of the deceased were also disputed.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents have supported the award passed by the Tribunal and submitted that the findings arrived at by the learned Tribunal are just and proper and does not require any interference by this Court under these appeals.

6. Heard the submissions and perused the record.
7.
On perusal of record it reflects that the learned Claims Tribunal has framed six issues in each of the claim cases.
Issue no. 1 is important to decide the present misc. appeals.

To prove this issue,
testimony of Dilip Kumar Dwivedi (PW-1) is important, as he is an injured eyewitness to the incident.
In his statement, he has NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:58392 4 MA-749-2016 specifically narrated the incident.

He has also stated that he sustained a facture in his right leg and soon after, was referred to Ambikapur, where he remained admitted till 21/05/2013 and thereafter remained hospitalized till 07/06/2013.
8. As per his statement (Exhibit-P/3), the report was registered within half hour of the incident.
An important fact which emerges from his statement is that the driver of the offending vehicle fled away from the place of accident soon after the incident.
He was not in a position to apprehend the driver as he suffered serious injuries and his colleague died on the spot.
The testimony of Dilip is collaborated by the testimony of Rajnish Pathak (PW-3), who is also an eyewitness and narrated the incident.

From the record of the case, this fact clearly reveals that the learned Trial Court has rightly dealt with issue no. 1.
9. Issue No. 4 pertains to the loss of income sustained by the claimants due to the said accident.
In Claim Case No.8 of 2013, the wife of deceased Meera Pandey (PW-1) exhibited documents relating to the income of the deceased.
Her testimony is supported by evidence of D.P Pathak (PW-4), who stated that the deceased was working as Chief Pharmacist in Bijuri Kalrai Hospital.
The salary certificate of the deceased is contained as Exhibited-P/10.
While deciding this issue, the multiplier has been rightly applied by the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:58392 5 MA-749-2016 Claims Tribunal and no amendment or correction is required.

10. In view of the aforesaid, this Court does not find any infirmity in the impugned order dated 06/10/2015 passed by the Claims Tribunal while deciding the Claim Case No.8 of 2013 and Claim Case No.9 of 2013.
11. Accordingly, both the Miscellaneous Appeals stand dismissed.
No order as to costs.
